name: Sharjah Islamic Bank
founded: 1975 (public joint stock company by Emiri Decree of the Ruler of Sharjah); fully converted to Islamic banking on 31 Mar 2002
ownership_summary: ADX-listed; the ultimate controlling party is the Government of Sharjah. At 30 Jun 2026 Sharjah Asset Management LLC held 25.00% and the Sharjah Social Security Fund 19.69%, both wholly owned by the Government of Sharjah; at 31 Dec 2025 the figures were 28.46% and 16.12% (S1, S2). Share capital rose from AED 3,235,677,638 to AED 4,314,236,850 through a rights issue of 1,078,559,212 shares at AED 2.40 (AGM approval 9 Mar 2026). The Government committed to take up its full entitlement (S1, S10, S11).

government_link: Yes. The Government of Sharjah is the ultimate controlling party, holding 44.69% through Sharjah Asset Management LLC and the Sharjah Social Security Fund at 30 Jun 2026 (S1).
group_structure: Sharjah Islamic Bank PJSC and wholly owned UAE subsidiaries: Sharjah National Hotels (hospitality), Sharjah Islamic Securities LLC SP (brokerage in local Shari'a-compliant shares, styled 'Sharjah Islamic Financial Services LLC (SIFS)' on the bank and subsidiary websites) and ASAS Real Estate LLC SP (real estate). Cayman SPVs SIB Sukuk Company III Limited and SIB Tier 1 Sukuk IIND Limited issue the bank's sukuk (S1, S6). The fully Islamic bank has no separately profiled subsidiaries.

footprint: UAE only: 35 branches at 30 Jun 2026, up from 34 at 31 Dec 2025 (S1). The 2025 ESG report lists 34 branches (17 in Sharjah City, 3 on the Sharjah East Coast, 5 in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, 7 in Dubai, 1 in Fujairah and 1 in Ras Al Khaimah), 152 ATMs, 80 CCDMs and 7 smart banking kiosks (S4). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Government and corporate (including high net worth individuals), retail (individuals and business banking), investment and treasury, and subsidiaries for hospitality, brokerage and real estate (S1, S4). The website shows no named affluent, priority or private-banking tier (S22).
business_lines: Four reported segments. Government & Corporate: AED 43.0bn of assets at 30 Jun 2026 and 37% of H1 2026 operating income. Retail: AED 5.7bn of assets (6%) and AED 139m (10%) of H1 2026 operating income. Investment & Treasury: AED 39.7bn of assets and 38% of income. Hospitality, Brokerage & Real Estate: 16% of income (S1). Treasury sells sukuk investment (with optional financing up to 3x), the 'SIB FX Investment' product, bespoke Shari'a-compliant structured products and customer Wakala deposits (S8). Brokerage on ADX and DFM runs through SIFS (S6, S13). A proprietary direct-investment book of AED 480m covers 18 holdings (S7).

capabilities.wealth_summary: SIB does not publish a wealth, priority or private-banking proposition. The personal-banking pages offer accounts, cards, financing and digital banking but no affluent tier, and the 'Wealth management' link on the Investment page is inactive. Retail is small: 6% of assets and about 10% of H1 2026 operating income. HNW individuals are served inside the Government & Corporate segment, with AED 3.38bn of HNW financing at 30 Jun 2026. Client investment products come from Treasury: sukuk investment with no leverage or up to 3x financing, 'SIB FX Investment' (an Islamic alternative to margin FX), bespoke Shari'a-compliant structured products and customer Wakala deposits. Local-share brokerage on ADX and DFM runs through the subsidiary Sharjah Islamic Securities / SIFS (est. 2005), which offers online trading and margin financing and released a 'SIFS Trading' iOS app on 19 Dec 2025. The SIB Digital banking app lists no investing features. No AUM, fund shelf, discretionary or model-portfolio offering was found.

private_banking.detail: No private-banking unit or page. The segment note says Government & Corporate 'includes exposure to high net worth individuals' (financing of AED 3.38bn at 30 Jun 2026).

asset_management.detail: No asset-management subsidiary or fund range. 'Direct Investment' is the bank's proprietary book: AED 480m across 18 holdings in listed and private equities, funds, alternatives and real estate.

brokerage.detail: Sharjah Islamic Securities LLC SP, branded SIFS (Sharjah Islamic Financial Services) and 100% owned since 2005. It is SCA-licensed and offers Shari'a-compliant share trading on ADX and DFM: NIN issuance, share transfers, margin financing, cash sweeps to SIB accounts and an online trading platform. SIB provides AED 100m guarantees each to ADX and DFM for its brokerage operations.

digital_investing.detail: Limited to local shares through SIFS. It offers an online trading platform and a 'SIFS Trading' app published by Sharjah Islamic Bank, with iOS v1.0 released 19 Dec 2025 offering Shari'a-compliant instruments in Arabic and English. The SIB Digital banking app lists payments, transfers and account opening but no investing.

advisory.detail: Treasury 'offers advisory and product solutions' to customers with profit-rate or FX exposure. This is hedging advisory, not a wealth advisory service.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: None found on the bank or SIFS sites.

funds_platform.detail: No mutual fund distribution pages found.

structured_products.detail: Treasury Client Solutions offers 'bespoke sharia`a compliant structured products for their investment needs'. The product range is not published.

private_markets.detail: No client access found. Private equity and alternatives sit only in the proprietary Direct Investment book.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Islamic bank. Client offerings include sukuk investment (unleveraged or with up to 3x financing), customer Wakala deposits (AED 31.2bn of deposits at 30 Jun 2026), Mudaraba investment deposits and Shari'a-compliant share brokerage through SIFS.

partners.what: The ESG report lists a 2021 'Infosys Finacle Innovation Award'. Use of Finacle as core banking system is not stated.

initiatives.what: Completed a rights issue of 1,078,559,212 new shares at AED 2.40 (net AED 2,583,542k credited to equity). Share capital rose to AED 4.31bn and CAR to 19.5%. Purpose: capital headroom and balance-sheet growth.
Launched a strategic rights issue of up to AED 2.59bn with Emirates NBD Capital as lead manager. The Government of Sharjah committed to its full pro-rata take-up.
Released the SIFS Trading iOS app (v1.0) for Shari'a-compliant trading through the brokerage subsidiary.
Digital onboarding grew 110% year on year (ESG report key highlights).

opportunities: No wealth, priority or private-banking proposition is published, and there is no fund shelf, discretionary or model-portfolio offering. The investment offer is limited to treasury sukuk/FX/structured products and local-share brokerage (S7, S8, S22).
HNW clients exist inside the corporate segment, with AED 3.38bn of HNW financing at 30 Jun 2026 (up from AED 2.83bn at Dec 2025), but no wealth service is described for them (S1).
The AED 2.58bn rights issue in May 2026 raised CAR to 19.5% to 'extend runway for balance sheet growth' (S3, S11).
The SIFS brokerage app is new (Dec 2025) and covers only UAE-listed Shari'a-compliant shares (S15, S13).
barriers: Islamic-only: every product must pass the Internal Sharia Supervision Committee, so Shari'a-screened portfolios and structures would be needed (S5).

Retail is a small business, with 6% of assets and about 10% of operating income, and the bank is weighted to government and corporate lending (AED 22.2bn of financing to government departments and authorities) (S1).
No public executive team, digital head or wealth head is named on the website, which makes entry points hard to identify (S18, S5).
Government-controlled (44.69%) and managed by a CEO in post since 2006–2007, so decision cycles may be conservative (S1, S17).

open_items: SIB publishes no executive management list on its website, and governance reports after 2021 are not on the IR page. The ADX filing of the 2025 governance report could not be downloaded (ADX blocks automated access, and a browser attempt triggered a file-save prompt that was not pursued). Heads of retail, treasury/investments, digital and SIFS are unidentified.
Customer numbers and absolute headcount are not disclosed in the opened sources.
